title: Sum of an Array
description:
You are given an array of whole numbers called `nums`. Return the total of all the numbers added together.

If the array is empty, the total is `0`.

Example: for `nums = [1, 2, 3]` the answer is `6`, because 1 + 2 + 3 = 6.

You only need to finish the `sum` method. We handle reading the input and printing your answer.
hints: Concept: an array is a row of boxes, each holding one number. You can visit every box with a loop, using `nums[i]` to read the box at position `i`.
Approach: keep a running total that starts at 0. Visit each number once and add it to the total. When the loop ends, the total is your answer.

Pseudocode:
  total = 0
  for each position i from 0 to length - 1:
      total = total + nums[i]
  return total

workedExample.title: Multiply Everything Together
workedExample.description: Given an array `nums`, return all the numbers multiplied together. For `[2, 3, 4]` the answer is `24`.
workedExample.explanation:
This is the **running total** pattern: one variable collects a result while the loop visits every element.

For multiplying, it starts at 1 (multiplying by 1 changes nothing). For adding, start at 0 (adding 0 changes nothing) and use `+` instead of `*`.

walkthrough.note: Start with total = 0. Nothing has been added yet.
i = 3 is not less than the length (3), so the loop stops. Return 6.

mistakes.hint: You stopped one number early. Use `i < nums.length` so the last number is included.
The loop goes one step too far. With `i <= nums.length`, the last pass reads a position that doesn't exist. Use `i < nums.length`.
This array is empty, so `nums[0]` doesn't exist. Start `total` at 0 instead of the first number.
